record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.context_brief: SU(1,1) WZW representation content and modular invariance
record.original_question: In the SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten conformal field theory, how should highest-weight current-algebra representations based on the discrete series and the continuous series be combined into a consistent, possibly non-unitary model whose operator product algebra and genus-one partition function satisfy modular invariance?

evidence.quote: Irreducible representations of the global algebra are essentially of two kinds: discrete D∓(j) or continuous principal Cp(b,a) and continuous supplementary Cs(j,a).
I now come to the following crucial question: How should the above representations be combined to form a consistent, though non-unitary, model?
The multiplicities NL,R must be chosen in such a way that the partition function is invariant under τ → τ + 1 and τ → −1/τ.

Another problem is related to the construction of various modular-invariant partition functions: What are the sets of representations – including representations based on both discrete and continuous series – which form a well-behaved OPA?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Wess–Zumino–Witten conformal field theory based on the non-compact group SU(1,1) (equivalently SL(2,R)) at level k. The irreducible unitary representations of the global SU(1,1) algebra fall into the following classes:

- Discrete lowest-weight series D^+(j) and discrete highest-weight series D^-(j), labeled by a real parameter j;
- Continuous principal series C_p(b,a), labeled by parameters b,a;
- Continuous supplementary series C_s(j,a).

These lift to highest-weight representations of the affine SU(1,1) current algebra at level k. Let S denote a set of such current-algebra highest-weight representations (allowed to include both discrete-series and continuous-series representations), and let N_{L,R} denote non-negative integer multiplicities pairing left- and right-moving representations to build the torus partition function
   Z(τ, τ̄) = Σ_{L,R ∈ S} N_{L,R} χ_L(τ) χ̄_R(τ̄),
where χ_L denotes the character of the corresponding current-algebra representation.

Problem. Determine all choices of the set S and multiplicities N_{L,R} such that:

1. The collection of primary fields associated with S closes under the operator product expansion, yielding a well-defined (possibly non-unitary) operator product algebra; and
2. The partition function Z(τ, τ̄) is invariant under the modular transformations τ → τ+1 and τ → -1/τ.

Classify the resulting consistent, possibly non-unitary, SU(1,1) WZW models obtained by combining discrete- and continuous-series representations in this way.
artifact.category_tag: SU(1,1) WZW models and modular invariance
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on SL(2,R)/SU(1,1) WZW models (notably by Maldacena–Ooguri and later authors) has produced explicit modular-invariant partition functions combining discrete and continuous (spectral-flowed) representations, particularly relevant to AdS3 string theory. However, a complete classification of all consistent operator product algebras and modular invariants mixing discrete and continuous series remains incomplete; the spectrum proposed by Maldacena–Ooguri is widely accepted as the physical one but a full ADE-type classification analogous to compact WZW models has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Non-holomorphic modular forms and SL(2,R)/U(1) superconformal field theory
status_evidence.snippet: For non-compact WZW models like SL(2,R), the partition function can be decomposed in terms of discrete and continuous representations, with non-holomorphic dependence in the continuous part.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: explicit modular-invariant partition functions mixing discrete and continuous SL(2,R) representations have been constructed.

status_evidence.title: A Unified Scheme for Modular Invariant Partition Functions of WZW Models
status_evidence.snippet: A unified method applied to WZW models at arbitrary level to systematically search for modular invariant partition functions.
status_evidence.claim: General schemes exist for compact WZW modular invariants but the non-compact SU(1,1) case is not fully classified.
